# DUM-SDK 0.16.0 Alpha

The first release with a stage in its version: `0.16.0-alpha`. Releases up to 0.15.2 kept plain `X.Y.Z` tags.

## Module publication

- `/dumsdk reload` no longer disconnects players in game. Each player whose catalog changed gets the new catalog in play; the client downloads the changed modules, turns off the old ones (and the modules that depend on them), starts the new ones and reloads module resources without reconnecting. Unchanged modules keep running. A changed server-scoped Fabric mod still disconnects the player with a request to restart the game; a failed or timed-out update, or a second publication during one, disconnects with the matching message.
- New Paper event `ClientModulesLoadedEvent`: modules that just started on a player's client, once on join (during `PlayerJoinEvent`) and again for the modules an update swapped. Server sides that send their module a state should send it here.
- Modules signed with the dev key are left out of the catalog with a warning, and players join without them, unless the new config option `allow-dev-signed: true` is set. A live server can no longer offer a jar that players' clients refuse.

## Versions and updates

- The mod and the plugin must have exactly the same version. A player with another version sees a window with both versions and the buttons Update and Cancel instead of a disconnect message. Only after Update does the mod download exactly the server's release from GitHub, older or newer, check its signature and replace itself when the game closes; the window offers to close the game.
- The mod no longer downloads updates by itself at game start. Check for updates in the DUM-SDK menu still installs the latest release on request.
- Versions carry their stage: `X.Y.Z-alpha` and `X.Y.Z-beta` (optionally `.N`) before the release `X.Y.Z`, in the tag, the file names and the release title.

## Diagnostics

- The client sends its own Fabric mods (top-level, as "id version") in HELLO. Paper logs them on join, with installation and update failures and with runtime failure reports; `ClientModuleFailureEvent.clientMods()` exposes them.

## Upgrade and validation

Protocol 7 with exact versions: update the client mod and the Paper plugin together, both to 0.16.0-alpha. A 0.15.x client is refused by a 0.16.0-alpha server with a text message naming both versions. Clients 0.15.x still have the old self-updater, which installs the latest release at the next game start, so they move to 0.16.0-alpha by themselves after one restart; later versions go through the new window. The publication messages are new keys (`core.updated`, `core.updated-selected`), so existing `messages.yml` files show the new text from the jar. A development server with dev-signed modules needs `allow-dev-signed: true` in `plugins/DUM-SDK/config.yml`.

Local macOS verification: the unit tests and `./gradlew build`; the client game test against a local Paper server with an in-game swap of sdktest, the swap of a module under its open screen with a resource reload, a second publication during an update, a timed-out update, a refused rollback and a cold mod added in game; the external publication stand through three phases with game restarts (hot updates, a cold mod installed and updated by the helper, a full reload); the version window against a plugin built as another version and a local stand-in for GitHub (Cancel downloads nothing, Update fetches exactly that release); a released 0.15.2 client on Windows against the macOS server before these changes. Not checked: a real self-update through GitHub to a stage version, Windows/Linux with this version, the players' full modpack and the live VDS.
